thesis: Maybank offers a defensible income return at 11.51x trailing earnings and a vendor-reported 6.2% yield, supported by nearly stable H1 profit and 15.657% CET1. The bull establishes measured distribution capacity without requiring earnings acceleration; declining income and rising gross impairment limit conviction but do not yet outweigh that compensation.
strongest_counterexample: Net operating income fell to RM14.611bn from RM15.397bn, gross impaired loans rose to RM9.362bn, and both capital ratios declined before the proposed dividend deduction; cost restraint may not indefinitely protect payout capacity.
invalidation_conditions: Reassess if the next comparable H1 attributable profit falls below RM5.171bn while net impaired loans exceed the observed 0.80% ratio.
Reassess if the next declared first interim dividend is below the observed 31 sen and post-distribution CET1 falls below 15.657%; compare capital on a consistent dividend basis.
decisive_factors: Stable H1 earnings and an increased declared interim payout support income ownership.
Capital is quantified and qualified for the dividend deduction; weak technicals affect entry timing rather than erase the income case.
